Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
The snapshot looks like spring 2015. Headline CPI is about 0% YoY, the unemployment rate is 5.5%, and the fed funds rate is about 0.13%. The dollar is up 13% YoY, which fits early-to-mid 2015.

The bond and gold moves narrow the month. The 10-year yield is 2.06%, up 0.38 over 3 months, which fits a rebound from the January 2015 low of about 1.68% to around 2.1% in May. Long Treasuries are down 3.4% over the month, which fits May 2015. Headline CPI at -0.02% YoY matches April 2015 (about -0.2%) or May 2015 (0.0%). Unemployment of 5.5% matches both March (5.5%) and May (5.5%), since April was 5.4%, and the published May figure was 5.5%.

Emerging-market equity is up 6.9% over 1 month, which fits April 2015 better than May. Developed ex-US equity is up 3.6% over 1 month, which also points to April. But 20y+ Treasuries fell 3.4% in April 2015 as well, with the 10-year yield moving from 1.92% to 2.03%. In May, the 10-year yield rose to 2.12%.

The VIX at 13.39 and payroll growth averaging 197k over 3 months are consistent with April or May. The March–April–May 2015 payroll average was weaker (about 200k in April, with March at 85k). I lean toward April 2015, though the 3-month change in payrolls (-127k) points to the 3-month average dropping from about 324k, which fits April.

If the 3m average payroll of 197k used April data, that would be (March 119 revised + Feb 265 + April 223)/3 ≈ 200k. That matches April well, so I'm choosing April.
